summary.text: A neuron, or nerve cell, is an electrically excitable cell that communicates with other cells by firing electric signals called action potentials.
Neurons receive and conduct impulses and pass them on through synapses, which commonly use tiny amounts of chemical neurotransmitters.
They form neural networks, mostly in the brain and spinal cord, and are the main components of nervous tissue in all animals except sponges and placozoans.

facts.label: Three types
facts.value: Sensory neurons, motor neurons and interneurons

facts.label: Axon length
facts.value: As far as 1 meter in humans, more in other species

facts.label: Cell body size
facts.value: Varies from 4 to 100 micrometers in diameter

facts.label: Who has none
facts.value: Plants and fungi do not have nerve cells

items.prompt: A neuron takes in messages from its neighbours and then passes its own message onward. Which part carries the outgoing message?
items.explain: Most neurons receive signals through the dendrites and soma and send signals out along the axon.

items.prompt: A neuron's voltage changes by a large enough amount in a short time. What does the neuron do?

options.label: Fires an all-or-nothing pulse that travels along its axon
Fires a pulse sized to match the change
Stores the change until the next day

items.explain: Past the threshold, the neuron generates an all-or-nothing electrochemical pulse called an action potential, which travels rapidly along the axon.

items.prompt: Your fingertip brushes something hot. Which type of neuron responds to the touch and sends signals toward the spinal cord?
items.explain: Sensory neurons respond to stimuli such as touch, sound or light and send signals to the spinal cord and then the brain.

items.prompt: One neuron's only job is to link two other neurons in the same region of the spinal cord. What type is it?
items.explain: Interneurons connect neurons to other neurons within the same region of the brain or spinal cord.

items.prompt: A gardener wonders whether a fern has nerve cells like a squirrel does. What is the answer?

options.label: Yes, but only in its roots
No, plants and fungi lack them
Yes, but they are much smaller
Only when it is growing in light

items.explain: Plants and fungi do not have nerve cells.

items.prompt: Someone hopes to grow lots of brand-new brain neurons in their fifties. According to the usual pattern, when are most neurons made?

options.label: At a steady rate throughout adult life
Mostly in old age to replace worn cells
Only during sleep at any age

items.explain: Neural stem cells generate most neurons during brain development and childhood, and neurogenesis largely stops in adulthood in most brain areas.
